Make post-production edits actually reach the rendered video

Edits applied through the studio reported success while the final cut came
back byte-identical, because each edit path lost its change somewhere between
the project state and the renderer:

- BGM style/query: node_music_search keyed its disk cache on the article text
  only, so a new style always hit the stale artifact. The key now includes the
  requested style, and bgm_query/bgm_volume are persisted in final_state.json
  so they survive a reload.
- BGM volume: the Tool_StitchVideo dispatch never forwarded bgm_volume or
  duck_under_voice to stitch_video.run, leaving the mix on its defaults.
- Subtitles: set_subtitle wrote shot["subtitle_text"] but the renderer only
  read vocal_script, so subtitle edits were silently dropped.
- Reorder/delete/volume-only edits produce no per-shot render steps, and the
  regeneration guard required a non-empty step list, so no job was scheduled
  at all. Tracked separately via restitch_dirty, which also disables the BGM
  fast remux: reordering preserves total duration, so the remux duration guard
  could not catch it and narration played against the wrong picture.
- swap_template accepted invented template ids, which the renderer resolves to
  a built-in default without complaining. Ids are now validated against the
  Gold Template library and the real registry is given to the chat agent.

Also fixes captions drifting out of sync with the voice-over: the agent was
attaching set_subtitle to template edits the user never asked to retext, and
because that op deliberately skips TTS the audience read a shortened script
while hearing the full one. set_narration now clears a stale override,
set_subtitle reports the divergence instead of a quiet success, and
subtitle_drift surfaces any remaining mismatch in the panel and the prompt.
swap_template accepts slots so a structure swap and its refill are one op.

Pin the deepagents harness to its upstream release tag

The harness version determines the action space the policy sees, so it is part
of the training contract rather than an interchangeable dependency. Install
deepagents from the upstream 0.7.7 tag (commit 42ed940) instead of the PyPI
package, so the tree is exactly the one the policy was developed against.

Verified equivalent to the vendored copy the tests ran against: that checkout
is an unmodified clone of langchain-ai/deepagents sitting 24 commits past the
0.7.7 tag, and the only change under libs/deepagents in those commits is one
line of tests/README.md — the shipped source and pyproject are identical.

Documented the constraint where it bites: aicut_agent/agent.py needs
HarnessProfile and register_harness_profile to strip the built-in tool suite,
so a version that reshapes those APIs fails to import rather than degrading
quietly. Noted the `pip install deepagents==0.7.7` equivalent for environments
without access to github.com.

Also ignore the scratch shot composites the renderer leaves in the template
root.

Initial public release of WeDirector

Long-horizon tool agent for end-to-end video editing: a 9B policy drives a
12-tool editing environment through a deepagents/LangGraph loop, with the
runtime as the single state authority so inference stays on the training
distribution.

Packaged for public release:

- Retrieval is now a pluggable extension point (pipeline/providers). Footage
  and BGM back ends can be added via config-only HTTP endpoints, local
  folders, or Python plugins, and the open-web provider is the default so a
  fresh clone works without any internal service.
- studio_config.yaml is the single configuration entry point, with ${VAR},
  ${VAR:-fallback} and an injected ${REPO_ROOT}. No module reads a hardcoded
  path, so `run_studio.sh --check` passes on a fresh clone with warnings only
  for the artifacts that are intentionally downloaded separately.
- Large binaries (Node, ffmpeg, headless Chrome, HyperFrames runtime, fonts)
  are excluded and fetched by scripts/setup_external_tools.sh, with manual
  instructions per component.
- Removed internal absolute paths, service addresses, and TTS credentials;
  every remaining external endpoint comes from config or the environment.

Docs: README (EN/ZH) plus architecture, configuration, providers,
external_tools and huggingface guides.
